newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Barrick wants mine on Chilean-Argentine border.
newsitem.headline: Barrick wants mine on Chilean-Argentine border.

text.p: Canada's Barrick Gold Corp, stepping up Argentine prospecting this southern summer, is considering a future gold mine straddling the Andean border with Chile, the firm's local chief said Tuesday.
Barrick Exploraciones Argentinas President Enrique Loncan told Reuters that the firm was planning to boost its exploration spending throughout Argentina.
"We calculate that total exploration spending will be about $8 million to $10 million, although this could vary depending on what we find," he said.

One of Barrick's chief targets will be the Lama prospect, just inside Argentina on the other side of the Andean mountain border from the firm's Pascua project in Chile. Barrick hopes that it will be able to extract any gold it finds in Lama as part of the same mining operation which will exploit Pascua.

Argentina and Chile, long jealous foes with a history of border disputes, have since become keen trading partners and are now working on a treaty to allow the free flow of mining goods and equipment across their borders.

But delays could result from the necessary approval of the treaty by both countries' parliaments. So the Chilean and Argentine governments are preparing joint-protocols, which do not need legislative approval, specifically giving the go-ahead for Pascua-Lama and the $500 million Pachn copper project being developed by Canada's Cambior.
"If the protocol goes through then we will start a very aggressive exploration campaign in the summer," Loncn said.
Under-Secretary for Mining Daniel Meiln said Monday the two protocols may be ready in October, as well as the draft treaty for congressional approval.

Loncn said that Barrick has already identified reserves of about six million ounces of gold in Pascua. "According to geological data, the mineralization could extend into Argentina." Even an extra million ounces or so on the Argentine side could make a joint-operation worthwhile, even if they were not part of the Pascua geological formation.
The Lama property covers around 5,000 hectares in the northwestern province of San Juan.

Barrick's Argentine project portfolio includes the Carmen prospect in San Juan province. Under an agreement signed with fellow Canadian company Argentina Gold in 1994, Barrick will invest at least $10 million exploring Carmen, in which it has a 60-percent share.
Barrick decided another Argentine prospect, Manantial Espejo in the highlands of the far southern region of Patagonia, was too small for it, Loncn said.
Triton, of Canada, has taken out an option agreement to buy 80 percent of the project.
